default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1028.title: Chandelier-exit flip follow
E-1028.hypothesis: A close that falls more than k average ranges below the rolling high is the break of a trailing stop that trend followers hold; their exits add to the move. Mirror for longs.

E-1029.title: Vortex indicator cross follow
E-1029.hypothesis: Upward vs downward vortex movement (distance from the prior bar's extremes over true range) shows which side is extending; a cross with a margin marks control passing to that side.

E-1030.title: Elder impulse colour flip follow
E-1030.hypothesis: When both the EMA slope and the MACD histogram slope point up, trend and momentum agree; the first bar of agreement is an entry for trend followers, and vice versa for shorts.

E-1031.title: Fisher transform turn from an extreme
E-1031.hypothesis: The Fisher transform stretches the price position in its rolling range; a turn of the line while it is far from zero marks the end of a one-sided push, so the next move is back toward the range middle.

E-1032.title: Index and dollar at the same extreme fade
E-1032.hypothesis: Index and dollar usually move inversely. When both make a new rolling high (or both a low) one of them is being pushed by flow that is not macro; the index leg tends to give back the move.

E-1033.title: Keltner channel close-outside follow
E-1033.hypothesis: A close more than k average ranges away from its EMA is a volatility-adjusted thrust that attracts momentum orders; follow it.

E-1034.title: Mean-median skew flip follow
E-1034.hypothesis: When the rolling mean of closes moves above the rolling median, recent large up moves are skewing the window: a thrust by an aggressive buyer; follow the flip (mirror for sells).

E-1035.title: Bar-to-bar gap and go
E-1035.hypothesis: A bar that opens beyond the prior bar's extreme and closes in the gap direction shows orders arriving with no resting liquidity to absorb them; follow.

E-1036.title: Previous clock-block range break follow
E-1036.hypothesis: The high/low of the just-finished 30/60/120 minute clock block is a level that many intraday traders watch; a close beyond it triggers stops and breakout orders.

E-1037.title: Regression-channel residual fade
E-1037.hypothesis: Price far from its rolling linear-regression line, in residual standard deviations, has overshot the local trend; it tends to snap back toward the line.
